Section 9 step 3 drafts the modules in the scaffold and graduates them; the dispatch placed them directly in the strict library (GFNBounds/Paper/), so the strict compile is the build itself.

throughAndProj also looks through a raw Expr.proj on `And` (besides And.left/And.right applications). The spec names only the applications; the raw form is the same projection, and admitting it changes no listed test.

isConjunctHead additionally excludes isAuxRecursor and isRecCore names. Redundant with the `theorem` kind test (casesOn/recOn are defs, recursors are recInfo), kept as a belt-and-braces reading of 'not a constructor or recursor'.

Error texts the spec leaves unspecified, chosen here: kind rejection 'paper: a placement must be global, not scoped or local'; erase 'paper: a placement cannot be erased'; bad syntax 'paper: expected `paper "<label>"`'; conjunctsOf on a non-theorem 'paper: conjunctsOf: <decl> is not a theorem'; on a bad head 'paper: conjunctsOf <decl>: the head <c> of a leaf is not a project theorem'; on a non-constant leaf 'paper: conjunctsOf <decl>: a leaf is not a constant application: <leaf>'. The bad-head message names the head constant rather than printing the leaf expression.

Section 3 says every expected message of section 8 is written relative to the test namespace. True for the #guard_msgs placement tests (validLabel, privTrue, Nat.add_comm print short). Not true for the conjunctsOf failure fixtures: their message is read in a catch through Exception.toMessageData.toString, which formats without the namespace context, so the expected strings there are fully qualified (GFNBounds.Paper.Test.f1, GFNBounds.Paper.Test.Pair.mk, ...).
Entry derives BEq in addition to Inhabited and Repr (used by the positive test's comparison through Prod). This adds instBEqEntry and instBEqEntry.beq to the new exported names.

Two tests beyond section 8: (a) after the positive block, `labels` on the module's environment is empty (nothing persists from withoutModifyingEnv); (b) a `rw` on the goal (Eq.mpr at the root) is refused by conjunctsOf, a case section 10 names. The `subst` in a branch (Eq.ndrec) case of section 10 is not a fixture.

The test module's own declarations are one private theorem (privTrue) and two private helper defs (expectConjuncts, expectConjunctsFail); all are `_private` names, skipped by isNoise and absent from lean-facts.json.

questions: Reading taken: the spec's 'not a constructor or recursor' is enforced by the theorem-kind test plus explicit isAuxRecursor/isRecCore exclusions. Whether casesOn-style auxiliary recursors on a Prop structure could ever be thmInfo was not exhaustively checked; the fixture shows Pair.casesOn is refused.

Reading taken: the label, not the label-and-item pair, is the key for duplicates. lem:x and lem:x.2 are distinct labels, so placing both on one declaration (as the positive test does) and lem:x.2 on another declaration than lem:x are both accepted; the spec does not say an item must sit on the same declaration as its statement.
kb_proposals: MessageData.ofConstName prints a name relative to the current namespace only when the message log renders it (what #guard_msgs compares); `(← e.toMessageData.toString)` on a caught exception prints the fully qualified name.
At Lean v4.31.0 a tactic-mode `have h := t; exact ...` leaves a non-dependent letE in the proof term (not a beta-redex), so stripping letE suffices for proof-term shape analysis.

Fixtures that declare theorems inside `run_cmd withoutModifyingEnv do elabCommand (<- `(theorem ...)))` under `set_option hygiene false in` leave nothing in the .olean or in lean-facts.json, and per-command linters (unused variables) do not run on them; this is how a strict-library test can declare throwaway project-namespace theorems.
